_comment: What blocks release, why (the requirement), and who resolves it. readiness.py holds no repository knowledge.

register.rule: every release gate passes, with its evidence in the register

ci.rule: K2: two distinct successful CI run IDs on the exact candidate SHA

trace_gaps.rule: every product requirement has an implementation

copy-branch.rule: logic decides on a configured value written in code

copy-fallback.rule: a configured value hard-coded as a fallback

copy-literal.rule: a configured value hard-coded as a literal

copy-embedded.rule: a configured value (such as the brand) embedded in code text or names; white-label

undeclared.rule: configuration read by code but declared nowhere

unread.rule: a declared setting nothing accesses (static evidence only)

unaccounted.rule: a configuration source neither declared nor classified

runtime-unread.rule: a traced setting no running code read during the test run (it may be read only in the browser, or not tested)

unwired-test.rule: a test no CI command runs

untested-module.rule: a module no test CI runs reaches

unowned.rule: a module with no owning domain

owner-lists-missing-file.rule: the ownership registry names a missing file

duplicate.rule: the same function body in two places (Knowledge Once)

trace-missing-path.rule: a traced implementation or test path does not exist

untraced-module.rule: a module no Master requirement traces (its requirements may live in the repository specifications)

outside-kernel.rule: an entity type stored outside the kernel (not derived through registry, entity, context, temporal and relationship)

environment-branch.rule: behaviour branches on which environment it runs in (an environment variable compared with a literal); read a declared setting the environment sets

environment-name.rule: an environment named in code; environments are open-ended registered configuration

agent-or-vendor-name.rule: an agent, assistant or vendor named in platform code; it belongs in a registry and is referenced by role or id

tooling-literal.rule: a literal in the Master's own tool code that looks like configuration (a file, path, identifier format, hash, date or number); it belongs in a registry

tests.rule: the full test chain passes on the exact candidate SHA, on a supported runtime, leaving the tree unchanged
